notes: Commercial APC propeller tested in UIUC Vol. 1 (Brandt 2005 / Brandt & Selig 2011, data ver. 3 with the 2015 motor-fixture drag correction). Geometry = APC's own design file (current release v2025-1001); APC revises designs, so the specimen tested in 2005-2008 may differ slightly: the UIUC PropellerScanner geometry of the tested specimen is in extraction/geometry_uiuc_scan.csv and is compared in extraction/check_uiuc_apcsp_11x7.png. Airfoils are KNOWN from the APC file (not assumed): APC file: AIRFOIL1 CLARK-Y at 2.00 in, AIRFOIL2 CLARK-Y at 3.00 in; anchors: clarky_t28p2 at r/R=0.153 (f=0.00, t/c=0.282); clarky_t24p0 at r/R=0.255 (f=0.00, t/c=0.240); clarky_t18p6 at r/R=0.442 (f=0.00, t/c=0.186); clarky_t15p8 at r/R=0.650 (f=0.00, t/c=0.159); clarky_t13p6 at r/R=0.858 (f=0.00, t/c=0.136); clarky_t12p0 at r/R=1.000 (f=0.00, t/c=0.120). ASSUMPTIONS in the airfoil model: (1) APC 'scales airfoils based on thickness ratio' - taken as thickness-only scaling (camber line kept); (2) the AIRFOIL1->AIRFOIL2 transition is a linear blend in r of camber line and thickness shape; (3) sections are modelled by a few XFOIL anchor sections with linear cl/cd transitions between them. Published BEM validations of APC thin-electric props used NACA 4412 outboard (McCrink & Gregory 2017: Clark-Y 0-5 % span, NACA 4412 elsewhere, from cutting the blades), consistent with APC's APC12 = NACA 4412. Polars: XFOIL Ncrit = 9 (UIUC tunnel Tu < 0.1 %), Ncrit = 5 alternatives listed. Rhub = first geometry station (0.15 R). Fluid: rho = 1.17 kg/m3, nu = 1.55e-5 m2/s assumed (UIUC lab, the database gives coefficients only). Chord Re at 0.75R ranges ~43k-85k (c75 = 20.9 mm, 0.75*Omega*R at the lowest/highest tested rpm).
